correctness.rationale: From paired-difference identities and exact cubic ODE, stationary pairs are symmetric. The first-group block has negative trace and determinant Delta>0 for u>1/2; the absent-group eigenvalue -1+beta*u crosses zero at beta=1/u. Invertible incumbent block, beta*c*(1-b)=1 and IFT give unique physical branch b=u*(beta-1/u)+O(eps^2) and negative small eigenvalue. At equality the center manifold has qc=1/Delta, qa=(1-u)/(u*Delta), yielding bprime=-b^2+O(b^3), t*b->1, t^2 feedback. A standalone symbolic/numerical check is supplied; finite tests are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The all-triple five-coordinate threshold and center-manifold response are not implied by inspected primary literature. St-Onge et al. study stochastic group AMEs, Cisneros-Velarde–Bullo continuous-time generic SIS Theorem 5.1 assumes irreducible pairwise mixing absent here, Cui et al. study direct/indirect pathways with different sufficient criteria, and Liang et al. analyze discrete-time sufficient stability. Known center-manifold methods are acknowledged, not asserted novel. Residual priority risk explicitly noted.
residual_risks: Older or poorly indexed exact local bifurcation calculation on a two-triangle pure-three-body contagion motif might exist.
A general continuous-time tensor model may imply portions of the local stability claim, but not the assessed combined physical critical feedback asymptotics on the inspected evidence.
The mathematical ODE is a mean-field closure and cannot be treated as exact finite-population Markov infection probabilities.
The general 2020 and 2023 continuous-time frameworks include some related tensor modeling, although their proved sufficient theorems do not entail this motif-level critical-amplitude package.

value.rationale: Provides a sharp, exact, natural local transition in a minimal overlapping-community higher-order contagion model. A weak second group can invade at beta_rec<2 despite lacking isolated persistence unless beta>=4. A universal critical slowdown b~1/t and quantified hub/first-group t^-2 response reveal observable recruitment transients, with a general support-ordering obstruction for stable localized states. Substantial enough to motivate motif-aware epidemic control; strict local/mean-field limitations disclosed.
